q: Mi wife and I started doing potty training last Friday right after nursery, after it being recommended by the nursery teacher. They believe that our son was ready for it.
cx: Father of a 26-month-old; nursery suggested starting.

q: Then today he went to the nursery again, where all the teachers are aware that he's off nappies  already. He held the pee all day and just at the very end, right before his mum picked him up, he had an accident and peed himself.
cx: First nursery day after a naked weekend at home.

q: I guess I just need some reassurance or understanding in order to accept that this is a normal phase in the process, and that we are not doing anything wrong or he is not ready. I truly believe he's ready and can accomplish it. I guess I just thought it would be a more linear process.
cx: Child cries at every pee on the potty in the first days.

q: Would you back off a few days and come back? Or hold off completely? How did you resume it?
cx: Asks commenters how a pause actually works.

q: Stickers don't work because then she wants more of them, resulting in a huge tantrum (trying not to create a negative association with the potty). I tried showing her a Sesame Street potty video and that also turned into a screaming fit because Elmo wasn't on screen the entire time.
cx: Two weeks into gentle potty introduction with a 25-month-old.

q: I know I just need to keep at it and keep some sort of routine but I feel so lost. I really want her potty trained before my second arrives at the end of August but I feel like I'm doing something wrong.
cx: Second baby due in August is the deadline.

q: Day 2, he didn’t have any accidents! He even went a pooped on the little potty. He peed on the potty all day, held it, knew when he needed to go. I thought we were pretty good..
cx: Naked method with a 3.5-year-old; good second day before day three fell apart.

q: All the books said it was par for the course, so we went on to day 4..
cx: Followed the books past a very hard day three.

q: My pediatrician told me to take a break for a bit, take the pressure off and come back to it later. That the naked method might be causing unnecessary stress..
cx: After a child panicked holding his pee during the naked method.

q: No one will care when he’s potty trained later, it’s not going to come up on a college application.. but I feel so behind. I’m a first time mom who’s feeling beyond defeated and I need any and all advice.. please. 😩
cx: First-time mother after the method failed.

q: Some parents can make passive aggressive comments like “wow he’s not very nice” or “wow he’s a lot today”. I even heard one mom say “he always seems nicer when mom isn’t around”.
cx: 22-month-old 'happy hitting' other kids at the playground.

q: Some of the other parents will tell me to just relax and let them be, kids will be kids, don’t stress so much. But 1/10 times he can actually hurt another kid and I don’t want that.
cx: Contradicting messages from other playground parents.

q: But sometimes I just feel like the biggest loser in the world. He seems like the only one who does this and I feel embarrassed and ashamed because he’s really truly a sweet boy.
cx: Mother who shadows him at every playground visit.

q: I’m 19 weeks pregnant with my second and already exhausted, I’m trying so hard to teach him to be gentle and protect the other kids without looking like a basket case but I’m clearly failing.
cx: Pregnant mother of a toddler who hits from excitement.

q: We were actually doing pretty good up until March when we bought a new house and on May 3rd we had a new baby. Since then she just hasn’t been easy to potty train because we can’t get her to be consistent.
cx: 2.5-year-old's casual training stalled after a move and a new baby.

q: We try to get her to use the potty by offering a reward (like candy) and sometimes she’ll go for it and other times not. She never asks to go potty on her own, I always have to convince her to sit on it.
cx: Rewards work only some of the time.

q: she goes to daycare during the day and while they do help with potty training, they seem to be pretty causal about it too.
cx: Daycare is as relaxed as the parents.

q: I’m a little frustrated because the daycare teacher said, “Your kids will all be potty trained by May.” My wife and I rolled our eyes when we heard that back in September.
cx: Three-year-old still uninterested in May.

q: We have tried everything: sticker charts, blowing bubbles, bribes. We tried the “Oh Crap!” method one weekend, and it was just awful—lots of tears. We haven’t pushed it for the last few months because we’ve been tired and don’t want to fight about it.
cx: Paused after one weekend of Oh Crap.

q: She wears pull-ups but still uses them like diapers. We also have a 1-year-old girl. Maybe she sees that the baby still gets to wear diapers and wants to be like her? I don’t know, but it’s been really hard and upsetting. I’m so sick of changing her.
cx: Two children in nappies.

q: We tried for a day on a weekend with no diaper and filled her full of juice. She just peed all over the floor and coach and cried the whole time.
cx: The no-diaper weekend.

q: My wife and I work full time jobs and can’t take 10 days off for her to be potty train.
cx: Reply to advice to stay home and train.

q: Lot’s very sound advice and support and lot’s of losers judging and trying to make me feel bad.
cx: Closing reply on the thread.

q: I browsed prior submissions but many of the posts were related to older toddlers.
cx: Looking for picky-eating help for an 18-month-old.

q: I sent him to school with a beautiful homemade enchilada (no special seasoning). I mean, it’s a soft tortilla, melted cheese and chicken. He won’t touch it.
cx: Parent who meal-preps; toddler now eats only a few foods.

q: I’m happy to just give him food he likes for the purpose of gaining weight but I don’t want to cause more picky eating.
cx: Weighing safe foods against making picky eating worse.

q: Do you think that interacting by playing with the food or counting it puts pressure on him? That’s what I’m trying to avoid
cx: Asks whether food play counts as pressure.
